title: Planning a Holiday Trip
description: Two friends plan a summer holiday

script.speaker: A
script.text: I'm thinking about visiting Italy this summer. Have you been there?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Yes, I went to Rome last year. It was amazing!

script.speaker: A
script.text: What's the best time to visit?

script.speaker: B
script.text: I recommend going in May or September. It's less crowded and not too hot.

script.speaker: A
script.text: How long did you stay?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Ten days. I visited Rome, Florence, and Venice.

script.speaker: A
script.text: That sounds wonderful. How much did you spend?

script.speaker: B
script.text: About fifteen hundred dollars including flights and accommodation.

questions.stemText: Where did Speaker B visit last year?
When does Speaker B recommend visiting?
Speaker B stayed for ___ days.
The trip cost about fifteen hundred ___.
Match cities with their country.

fullScript:
A: I'm thinking about visiting Italy this summer. Have you been there?
B: Yes, I went to Rome last year. It was amazing!
A: What's the best time to visit?
B: I recommend going in May or September. It's less crowded and not too hot.
A: How long did you stay?
B: Ten days. I visited Rome, Florence, and Venice.
A: That sounds wonderful. How much did you spend?
B: About fifteen hundred dollars including flights and accommodation.

title: At the Restaurant — Complaining
description: A customer complains about food at a restaurant

script.speaker: A
script.text: Excuse me, I ordered the steak but this is chicken.

script.speaker: B
script.text: Oh, I'm very sorry about that. Let me fix that for you.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Also, my soup is cold. It should be hot.

script.speaker: B
script.text: I apologize. I'll bring you a new soup immediately.

script.speaker: A
script.text: And my friend is still waiting for her salad. It's been thirty minutes.

script.speaker: B
script.text: I'm so sorry for the delay. I'll speak to the kitchen right away.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Thank you. We'd also like some more bread please.

script.speaker: B
script.text: Of course. And your meal tonight is on the house. No charge.

questions.stemText: What did the man order?
What is wrong with the soup?

The waiter says the meal is on the ___.

title: Talking About Hobbies

script.speaker: A
script.text: What do you usually do in your free time?

script.speaker: B
script.text: I love photography. I take photos every weekend.

script.speaker: A
script.text: That's interesting! What kind of photos do you take?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Mostly nature and street photography. I have a blog with five hundred followers.

title: Health and Exercise
description: A doctor talks to a patient about exercise habits

script.speaker: A
script.text: How often do you exercise, Mr. Chen?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Not very often, doctor. Maybe once or twice a week.

script.speaker: A
script.text: What kind of exercise do you do?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Usually walking. Sometimes I go swimming on weekends.

script.speaker: A
script.text: I recommend at least thirty minutes of exercise five times a week.

script.speaker: B
script.text: That sounds like a lot. What kind do you suggest?

script.speaker: A
script.text: Cycling is excellent. It's easy on the joints and very effective.

script.speaker: B
script.text: OK, I'll try to cycle to work. It's only four kilometers.

questions.stemText: How often does Mr. Chen exercise now?
What exercise does the doctor recommend?
The doctor recommends ___ minutes of exercise.
Mr. Chen's workplace is ___ kilometers away.
Match exercise type with description.

fullScript:

B: Not very often, doctor. Maybe once or twice a week.
A: What kind of exercise do you do?
B: Usually walking. Sometimes I go swimming on weekends.
A: I recommend at least thirty minutes of exercise five times a week.
B: That sounds like a lot. What kind do you suggest?
A: Cycling is excellent. It's easy on the joints and very effective.
B: OK, I'll try to cycle to work. It's only four kilometers.

title: Using Public Transport
description: A tourist asks about public transport options

script.speaker: A
script.text: Excuse me. I need to get to the airport. What's the best way?

script.speaker: B
script.text: You can take the train or the bus. The train is faster.

script.speaker: A
script.text: How long does the train take?

script.speaker: B
script.text: About thirty minutes. The bus takes over an hour in traffic.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Where do I catch the train?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Central Station, just two blocks from here. Take the yellow line.

script.speaker: A
script.text: How much is the ticket?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Twelve dollars one way. You can buy it at the ticket machine.

title: Making an Appointment
description: A patient calls to make a doctor's appointment

script.text: Good afternoon, Dr. Smith's office. How can I help?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Hello, I'd like to make an appointment to see Dr. Smith.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Is this for a regular check-up or is it urgent?

script.speaker: B
script.text: It's not urgent. I've had a cough for two weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.text: I see. We have an opening on Thursday at three o'clock.

script.speaker: B
script.text: Is there anything earlier? I prefer mornings.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Tuesday at nine thirty is available.

script.speaker: B
script.text: Perfect. My name is Robert Green. Can you text me a reminder?

title: At the Bank
description: A customer opens a bank account

script.speaker: A
script.text: Good morning. I'd like to open a bank account.

script.speaker: B
script.text: Of course. We have checking and savings accounts. Which would you prefer?

script.speaker: A
script.text: What's the difference?

script.speaker: B
script.text: A checking account is for daily use. A savings account earns more interest.

script.speaker: A
script.text: I'll open a savings account. What do I need?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Your passport and proof of address. And a minimum deposit of one hundred dollars.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Can I also get internet banking?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Yes, it's free with all accounts. I'll set it up for you today.

script.text: What about transport?

script.text: Sounds ideal. Is it expensive to live there?
